steps.what: Attend lectures, follow the instructor's explanations and note points relevant to supporting students

tasks.design: Retain lecture attendance with the assistant. Materials in {LMS} can complement attendance, but a summary does not establish that observing the instructor and following the class can be removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task includes learning the instructor's emphasis and students' immediate context.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated replacement for attendance is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Questions and examples arising in class may shape later support.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what students found confusing and align subsequent assistance with the lecture.
tasks.altitude: Attendance and learning responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: How lecture emphasis connects to later discussion groups

evidence.claim: Keeping attendance fully counted is an E1 design judgement; no attendance-replacement saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant attendance, excluding the instructor's delivery labour and separate material preparation.
No structured transcript or automated summary is assumed.
No new tool or upkeep is proposed, so native configuration is unnecessary.
research_questions: What aspects of live attendance are required for effective later student support?

already_counted.description: All lecture attendance and learning retained

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0. No lecture time is replaced by an assumed summary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange supervisor teaching observations and feedback

steps.what: Agree observation purpose, suitable teaching sessions and supervisor availability
Coordinate observation and feedback appointments and prepare invitations
Verify arrangements, send invitations and confirm the feedback process with the supervisor

tasks.design: Use native availability views and paired appointment templates in {CALENDAR} for the observation and feedback discussion. The assistant still agrees the purpose and checks the exact arrangements before sending invitations; no teaching-performance assessment is automated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated availability messages can dominate straightforward appointment coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Native calendar views and reusable invitations can reduce that exchange.
tasks.still_hard: A suitable observation requires the right session, supervisor and agreed feedback expectations.
tasks.human_edge: Create a constructive feedback arrangement rather than treating observation as a score.
tasks.altitude: Less scheduling exchange, with unchanged responsibility for arranging meaningful feedback.

evidence.claim: Calendar availability reuse and the proposed coordination saving are E1 design assumptions; the digest has no measured observation-scheduling case.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant arrangement work only. Supervisor observation and feedback delivery and assistant participation in those sessions are separate unchanged activities, not hidden savings.

Assistant captures session reference, duration, possible dates, location, supervisor identity and feedback format in s1, retaining all 35 hours. Supervisor maintains their existing calendar; no new availability reporting is requested.

s2 consumes those captured constraints and existing availability only. Missing calendar access or uncertain suitability requires manual messages in retained s2 time; the calendar does not choose teaching quality criteria.
Test native scheduling first. Two focal upkeep hours cover invitation and access settings.
unknowns: Shared calendar access and local observation procedure
research_questions: Can native scheduling reduce coordination by 60% after exceptions and invitation checks?

incremental.description: Maintain paired invitation template and access

approvals.approved_version: Final observation and feedback invitations with session, dates, durations, location, attendees and purpose; changes void approval before sending

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85, gross=15 minus 2 upkeep gives net=13. High assumes shared availability; low assumes only 2 coordination hours saved. Purpose agreement and final confirmation retain 75 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assist instructors in using audiovisual equipment and troubleshoot practical setup problems

tasks.design: Keep in-room audiovisual assistance with the assistant. Existing equipment guidance in {DOCS} supports the work, but does not demonstrate a reduction in explanation, connection checks or troubleshooting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment problems depend on actual room state and the instructor's immediate needs.
tasks.enabler_now: No matching change to physical assistance is established.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected faults and unfamiliar controls require direct help or technical escalation.
tasks.human_edge: Explain calmly while checking that the instructor can continue teaching.

reach.learn: How to explain reliable setup and when to call technical support

evidence.claim: Retaining direct audiovisual support in full is an E1 task design, without a time saving claim.

assumptions: Boundary is immediate instructor assistance; specialist repairs and separate equipment procurement are excluded.
No structured fault code or automated diagnosis is assumed; identifying the problem remains in s1.
No new guidance programme or software is introduced, so native configuration and incremental upkeep are zero.
unknowns: Equipment mix and technical escalation arrangements
research_questions: Which faults require specialist support rather than assistant troubleshooting?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0 and net=0; no separate documentation baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Gather authorised course records and selected student work for the conference
Assist faculty during student conferences, clarify facts and support agreed follow-up

tasks.design: Configure a source-linked conference pack in {LMS} and {DOCS} using existing authorised records. Keep student discussion, faculty decisions and agreed follow-up human; no student risk or performance judgement is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Selected records may be collected repeatedly across course folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native course links can group existing work and records for review.
tasks.still_hard: A student's concerns may not be explained by the available course records.
tasks.human_edge: Listen without prejudging the student and support the faculty member's response.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less record collection, with unchanged support and decision boundaries.

evidence.claim: Native source-linked conference packs and their proposed collection saving are E1 design assumptions; no matching measured case is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is assistant preparation and conference support; faculty and student time are outside the focal denominator and unchanged.

Faculty produces conference purpose and selects relevant course records in the existing brief; students and markers produce existing work and recorded results. Assistant selects student and course references, checks authorisation and links sources in retained s1 time. No free structured concern or risk label is assumed.
Missing or mismatched records require manual collection in retained s1 time; no automated summary changes their meaning.
Test native record links before code. Two focal upkeep hours cover pack links and access controls.
unknowns: Assistant record access and conference purpose
research_questions: Can linked records cut collection by 40% without reducing confidentiality checks or conference participation?

already_counted.description: Record selection, authorisation and manual fallback

incremental.description: Maintain conference links and access settings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=92, gross=8 minus 2 upkeep gives net=6. High assumes reusable authorised links; low assumes only 2 collection hours saved. All 80 conference-support hours remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Scheduling and record collection may shrink; learning from lectures and supporting people remain central.
reach: Postsecondary teacher: constructive observation and student support
role.ambitious_version: Provide dependable teaching support while preserving direct attention to instructors and students.
